exact_statement: For every finite private priority list of pairwise disjoint point-test control blocks selecting independent pairwise disjoint Boolean data cores with default +1, every finite adaptive physical restriction tree permits arbitrary control query order and arbitrary data interruptions and satisfies H(F_root)<=U_root+R_root+(3/ln2)T_data+K_ctrl Pi_ctrl+E[H_leaf-U_leaf-R_leaf], where K_ctrl=6+(5+ln10)/ln2<17 bits per influence, U=sum q_j[H(u_j)-eta((Eu_j)^2)], R=sum eta(q_j)Var(u_j), T_data=sum w q_j beta_j^2, and Pi_ctrl is same-tree actual controller influence spent. At controller-resolved leaves H-U-R=eta((Eu_leaf)^2)<=I_leaf/ln2. There is no bound on number of tests, widths or physical tree depth. A single common activation bit with all events in the same orientation is included in arbitrary order by adding a first private point test selecting the constant default. For a queried point test behind independent earlier Boolean event blocks (not necessarily point events), the normalized squared failure-guard spectrum has a last-nonempty-frequency tail t_J with E ln(1/t_J)<=1-e, and the same local controller payment applies. Inherited core entropy and unresolved terminal costs are retained. The previously reviewed version1 stronger ordered-priority coefficient8+2/ln2 remains valid at its original scope.
